name: Chyasalin mandap
description:
Heritage Site The octangular Chyasalin mandap pavilion is not a temple, despite the fact that most people mistake it for one.
Despite the fact that it is only a pavilion, it is one of the most stunning constructions of the Malla era. The kings of Bhaktapur, however, were not responsible for its construction. The entire credit goes to King Srinivas Malla, the then-King of Lalitpur who erected it as a sign of friendship.
Aside from that, there is an intriguing story concerning the Chyasalin mandapâ€™s construction, which explains why it was built between the Pashupatinath temple and the 55-window palace. There is a Hindu concept that one should not live in front of the glorious deity.
And living directly in front of the Pashupatinath shrine was bad for both the king and the kingdom. Thus, Chyasalin Mandap is reported to be built in between them to avoid the templeâ€™s powerful aurora from directly striking the palace.
This venue once was also a popular choice for the poetry contest. According to published knowledge, King Bhupatindra Malla and his consort once held a poetry competition at this spot.
This pavilion was also used to welcome royal guests, observe festivals, and enjoy the breathtaking sunset views.
Unfortunately, it was destroyed by the catastrophic earthquake of 1934 A.D. and lost its original form. Later, in 1992 A.D., the German architects graciously reinstall this covering at its original speed. They used steel and the ruins of the old chyasalin mandap there. As a result, it was completely impervious to the April 2015 earthquake.

name: Uma Maheshwor Temple
description:
Religious Site It is said that Bishwo Nath (source) from Patan (made endowments to) built this temple and installed idols of Bhawani Shankar which is now known as Bhawani Shankar Uma Maheshwor. The idol was installed in respect of Shiva and his concort Parvati, both immensely worshipped by Hindus.Inside the temple, inscriptions dated 1662 AD, 1678 AD, 1679 AD, 1687 AD 1715 AD (782 NS, 798 NS, 779 NS, 807 NS and 835 NS) can be found. Idols of Saraswati, Maheshmardini and Ganesh are also placed inside temple.

Architectural Characteristics
The temple stoods as an example of extraordinary Newah temple architecture. This three tiered temple rests on a raised platform of four successive plinths made of brick.A stone stairway leads to ground floor of temple where a circumambulatory space is also provided in the form of Verandah. Two elephants in the first plinth guard the entry way. Inner core brickwall and twenty number of beautifully carved exterior columns support the upper structure. Just below the first roof, a verandah like space is provided instead of solid wall normally seen in other temples.The brick walls are provided with decorated doors and windows. All the three roofs are finished with jhingati tiles and supported from below by decorative timber struts. The struts consists of images of gods/goddesses. The temple is topped by metal gajur and a metal banner is hanged down from gajur to first tier in the front side. As Uma Maheshwor temple is located in high elevation, it provides the good views of Kathmandu and immediate surroundings.

name: Rudraman Gurung Memorial Park
description:
Rudrabarna Mahabihar, also known as Uku Bahal, is a historic Buddhist monastery situated in Patan, Nepal. Located south of Patan Durbar Square, this monastery is renowned for its well-preserved Newar Buddhist architecture and rich cultural heritage.

Historical Significance

The monastery was established by King Sivadev I of the Lichhavi dynasty and has been referenced in various ancient texts. It holds cultural and religious importance for the local Newar community, particularly the Shakya clan, who perform daily worship rituals here. Notably, every male member of the Shakya clan is required to serve as a priest at the bihar for at least two weeks once in his lifetime.

Architectural Features

Rudrabarna Mahabihar is distinguished by its exquisite architecture, including:

- A central courtyard adorned with a large white stupa.

- Four corners featuring statues of deities.

- A spacious courtyard called Tago Chiba, surrounded by rows of houses, creating a communal atmosphere.

The monastery is also home to numerous metal artworks and intricately carved windows, reflecting the artistic prowess of the Newar community.

Visitor Experience

Visitors to Rudrabarna Mahabihar can explore its serene courtyards, observe traditional rituals, and appreciate the intricate craftsmanship of the Newar artisans. The monastery offers a glimpse into the spiritual and cultural life of the local community.



A visit to Rudrabarna Mahabihar provides a profound insight into Nepal's Buddhist heritage and the enduring traditions of the Newar people.

name: Kapilvastu Museum
description:
Kapilvastu Museum, situated in Tilaurakot, Nepal, is a cultural and religious institution dedicated to preserving the rich history of the ancient city of Kapilvastu, the birthplace of Siddhartha Gautama, who later became known as the Buddha. The museum houses a diverse collection of artifacts, including terracotta vessels, copper coins, and other items dating back to the 7th century BC, offering valuable insights into the region's archaeological and cultural heritage.The museum's exhibits are meticulously curated to showcase the art and artifacts discovered at various archaeological sites within the ancient Kapilvastu territory, such as Tilaurakot, Niglihawa, Gotihawa, Arorakot, Sisahaniyakot, Chhetradehi, Sagrahawa, and Pipari. These sites have yielded numerous ancient art remains and monuments, many of which are on display at the museum, providing visitors with a comprehensive understanding of the area's historical significance.Visitors to the Kapilvastu Museum can explore its well-organized galleries, which feature a range of artifacts that illuminate the daily life, religious practices, and artistic achievements of the ancient inhabitants of Kapilvastu. The museum serves as an essential resource for scholars, students, and tourists interested in the history of Buddhism and the cultural evolution of the region.

For those planning a visit, the museum is located approximately 26 kilometers from Lumbini, the birthplace of Lord Buddha, making it a convenient addition to a pilgrimage or cultural tour of the area.

Accessibility: Syange is accessible via the Annapurna Circuit trekking route, with the waterfall being a notable landmark along the way.

Best Time to Visit: The ideal times to visit are during the dry seasons, from October to April, when the weather is favorable for trekking and outdoor activities.

Accommodation: Basic lodging options are available in the village of Syange, offering trekkers a place to rest and refresh.

name: Kumakh Hill
description:
Kumakh Hill, situated at an elevation of approximately 2,520 meters above sea level, is a prominent natural and religious site in Salyan District, Nepal. It serves as a significant destination for both pilgrims and tourists, offering panoramic views of the surrounding landscapes.

Key Features:

Siddha Temple: At the summit of Kumakh Hill lies the Siddha Temple, a revered site for devotees. The temple is particularly significant during the Kojagrat Purnima, a full moon day, when a fair is held, attracting numerous visitors.

Caves: The hill is home to several caves, with the Siddha Cave being notably beautiful. These caves are not only natural attractions but also hold religious importance, with devotees often visiting to worship.

Panoramic Views: From the top of Kumakh Hill, one can observe views of 15 districts, including nearby villages, various terrains of the Terai, and prominent hills such as Sisne, Dhaulagiri, Chakhura Kumakh Hill, Chakhure Hill, Digre, and Bhagwati Temple.

Cultural Significance:

The fair held during Kojagrat Purnima is a vibrant event where traditional dances like Bangadi, Tappa, Sorthi, Passeri, Dohori, and Serenge are performed, reflecting the rich folk culture of the local communities.

Visiting Information:

Accessibility: Kumakh Hill is accessible by an eight-hour trek from the district headquarters of Salyan, Khalanga.

Best Time to Visit: The ideal time to visit is during the dry season, from October to April, when the weather is pleasant, and the hill is in full bloom.

name: Baarahi A jima Temple
description:
The Barahi Ajima Temple, also known as "Yakati Ajima" in Nepalbhasa, is a significant religious site located in Bhaktapur, Nepal. Situated near the Araniko Highway, just west of the Suryabinayak crossing, this temple holds substantial cultural and spiritual importance for the local community.

Historical and Cultural Significance:

Barahi Ajima is revered as the female counterpart of Lord Vishnu's boar incarnation, Lord Baraha. According to local traditions, the goddess Barahi was created on the fifth day of Nawaratri, a festival dedicated to the worship of the nine forms of the goddess Durga. The temple is part of the Astamatrika Mandala, which encompasses eight mother goddesses and is integral to the Nawaratri celebrations in Bhaktapur.

Architectural Features:

The temple showcases traditional Newari architecture, characterized by intricate wood carvings and a tiered pagoda-style roof. Its proximity to the Araniko Highway makes it easily accessible to visitors.

Festivals and Rituals:

During Nawaratri, devotees flock to the temple to offer prayers and seek blessings. The temple also hosts various ceremonies, including the preparation of 'samay baji'—a traditional Newari ritual platter—during special occasions. 

Visitor Experience:

Visitors to the Barahi Ajima Temple can immerse themselves in the rich cultural heritage of Bhaktapur. The temple's serene environment, coupled with the vibrant local traditions, offers a unique experience for those interested in Nepalese culture and spirituality.

name: Baala Falls
description:
Baala Falls, also known as Baala Jharana, is a picturesque waterfall located in Bardev, Konjyosom, Lalitpur, Nepal. Situated approximately 25 kilometers southeast of Kathmandu, this natural attraction offers visitors a serene environment to relax and enjoy the beauty of nature.

Features and Experiences:

Natural Swimming Pool: The base of the waterfall forms a natural pool, making it an ideal spot for swimming and cooling off, especially during the warmer months.

Scenic Beauty: Surrounded by lush greenery and tranquil surroundings, Baala Falls provides a peaceful retreat from the city's hustle and bustle.

Photography Opportunities: The cascading waters and verdant backdrop offer excellent opportunities for photography enthusiasts.

Visitor Information:

Accessibility: Baala Falls is accessible via a short hike from the nearest road. Visitors should be prepared for a moderate walk through natural terrain.

Facilities: Basic amenities are limited in the immediate vicinity of the falls. It's advisable to carry essentials such as water and snacks.

Best Time to Visit: The waterfall is most impressive during the monsoon season (June to September) when the water flow is at its peak. However, the area remains accessible year-round.

Nearby Attractions:

Phulchoki Hill: Located nearby, Phulchoki Hill is the highest point in the Kathmandu Valley, offering panoramic views and hiking trails.

Kushadevi Temple: A revered Hindu temple situated in the vicinity, attracting pilgrims and visitors alike.

name: National Art Gallery
description:
The National Art Gallery in Bhaktapur, Nepal, is a prominent cultural institution dedicated to preserving and showcasing Nepalese art. Established in 1960 by the Government of Nepal's Department of Archaeology, the gallery is housed in the historic Simhadhwaka Durbar (Lion Gate Palace), built by King Bhupatindra Malla in 1697 AD. 

Collections and Exhibits:
- Paintings:The gallery features an extensive collection of Tantric cloth paintings, known as Paubhas, which are the Hindu counterparts to Buddhist thangkas. These artworks depict various deities and religious narratives. 

- Sculptures and Artifacts:Visitors can explore a variety of sculptures and artifacts, including metal, stone, and wooden votive objects, some dating back to the 12th century. 

- Manuscripts: The gallery also houses ancient palm-leaf manuscripts, offering insights into Nepal's rich literary heritage. 

Visitor Information:

- Location:Situated in Bhaktapur Durbar Square, the gallery is easily accessible to visitors exploring the historic area.

- Ticketing:A single ticket grants access to the National Art Gallery, the Woodcarving Museum, and the Brass & Bronze Museum in Tachupal Tole. 

- Operating Hours:The gallery is typically open daily from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. It's advisable to check the latest timings before planning your visit.

For art enthusiasts and those interested in Nepalese culture, the National Art Gallery offers a comprehensive and enriching experience, reflecting the country's artistic legacy.

name: Bannigadhi jayagadha
description:
Bannigadhi Jayagadh is a rural municipality located in Achham District, Sudurpashchim Province, Nepal. It encompasses an area of 58.26 km² and has a population of approximately 17,359 residents. 

Key Features:

Geographical Location: Situated in the far-western region of Nepal, Bannigadhi Jayagadh offers visitors a glimpse into rural life and natural landscapes.

Cultural Significance: The area is known for its traditional customs, festivals, and community events that reflect the rich cultural heritage of the region.

Natural Beauty: The municipality is surrounded by scenic views, including forests and rivers, providing opportunities for eco-tourism and nature exploration.

Visitor Experience:

Community Engagement: Visitors can participate in local festivals and cultural events, gaining insights into the traditions and lifestyles of the inhabitants.

Nature Exploration: The natural surroundings offer opportunities for hiking, bird watching, and photography, especially in areas like the nearby forests and rivers.

Practical Information:

Accessibility: Bannigadhi Jayagadh is accessible via road from major cities in the Sudurpashchim Province. Travelers should plan their journey accordingly, considering the rural infrastructure.

Accommodation: Basic lodging options are available within the municipality, with more extensive facilities in nearby towns.

Best Time to Visit: The ideal time to visit is during the dry season, from October to April, to enjoy favorable weather conditions.

name: Bhimsensthan : Bhin Dyo Temple
description:
The **Bhimsensthan Temple**, also known as **Bhin Dyo Temple**, is a significant Hindu shrine located in the heart of Kathmandu, Nepal. Dedicated to **Lord Bhimsen**, the deity revered for his strength and protection, the temple holds a special place in the cultural and spiritual life of the local community.

**Key Features:**

- **Deity:** The temple is dedicated to **Lord Bhimsen**, a deity worshipped for his strength and protection, particularly by traders and merchants who seek his blessings for success in their business ventures.

- **Historical Significance:** The temple has deep historical roots and is associated with the life of **Bhimsen Thapa**, a prominent Prime Minister of Nepal during the early 19th century. His legacy is intertwined with the temple's importance in local culture.

- **Architecture:** Bhimsen Temple features traditional Nepali architecture, characterized by intricate wood carvings and detailed stonework that reflect the artistic heritage of the Malla period.

- **Cultural Importance:** The temple serves as a vital community hub where various religious activities and festivals are celebrated, fostering a sense of unity among local worshippers.

**Visiting Information:**

Situated in Kathmandu, the temple is easily accessible for both locals and tourists exploring this historic area known for its rich cultural heritage. Visitors can immerse themselves in the spiritual ambiance and appreciate the intricate craftsmanship of the temple's architecture.

name: Dhap Dam , Shivapuri National Park
description:
Dhap Dam is a man-made reservoir situated within the Shivapuri National Park, approximately 26 kilometers from Kathmandu, Nepal. Constructed in 2010, the dam was designed to enhance the flow of the Bagmati River during the dry season by capturing and storing monsoon rainfall. 

Key Features:

Dimensions: The dam stands 24 meters tall and spans 175 meters in width, with a maximum water storage capacity of 850,000 cubic meters. 

Ecological Significance: Located within Shivapuri National Park, the area is rich in biodiversity, offering opportunities for wildlife observation and nature walks. 

Visitor Information:

Activities: Visitors can enjoy hiking, bird watching, and photography, with the serene environment providing a peaceful retreat from the city. 

Access: The hike to Dhap Dam begins at the Sundarijal entrance of Shivapuri National Park. The trail is approximately 14 kilometers from Kathmandu and typically takes 3 to 5 hours to complete, depending on pace and route. 

Fees: Entrance fees for the park vary based on nationality:

Nepali Citizens: 100 NPR

SAARC Citizens: 600 NPR

Foreigners: 1,000 NPR per person, plus an additional 1,500 NPR per group for a required guide. 

Best Time to Visit:

The ideal time to visit is during the dry season, from October to April, when the weather is clear and the trails are accessible.

For more detailed information and planning your visit, you may refer to local tourism resources or contact local tour operators specializing in the area.

name: Ibahi Thura stupa
description:
The stupa Ibahi Thura, also known as the Northern Ashokan Stupa, located in Patan, Nepal. This stupa is one of the four Ashokan stupas that demarcate the ancient boundaries of Patan, believed to have been erected by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.

Key Features of Ibahi Thura:

Perimeter and Structure: The stupa has a perimeter of 60.62 meters. It features a vedika (railing) of 1.5 meters in height and a dome rising to 5.5 meters. Atop the dome sits a square harmika, crowned with a 13-step cakravali and a yasti (spire) 

.

Buddha Images: The vedika houses five Buddha images with their consorts, with the exception of Tathagata Vairocana 

.

Architectural Resemblance: The structure bears similarity to the Swayambhunath Stupa in Kathmandu, noted for its complexity compared to the other three Ashokan stupas in Patan 

.

Historical Context:

Emperor Ashoka, a prominent proponent of Buddhism, is credited with constructing these stupas during his visit to the Kathmandu Valley. The four stupas—Lagan Thura (South), Teta Thura (East), Pucho Thura (West), and Ibahi Thura (North)—serve as historical markers of Patan's ancient city limits and reflect the rich Buddhist heritage of the region 

.

Visiting Ibahi Thura:

Situated in the northern part of Patan, Ibahi Thura is accessible to visitors interested in exploring Nepal's ancient Buddhist architecture. Its resemblance to the Swayambhunath Stupa offers insights into the architectural styles prevalent during Emperor Ashoka's era.

name: Chankheli Pass
description:
Chankheli Pass, situated at an elevation of approximately 3,308 meters (10,853 feet) in Nepal's Karnali Province, serves as a vital link between the Mugu and Humla districts. This mountain pass is renowned for its challenging terrain and breathtaking vistas, making it a notable destination for trekkers and adventure enthusiasts. 

**Geographical Significance:**
The pass connects the remote regions of Mugu and Humla, facilitating access to areas that are otherwise difficult to reach. Its strategic location has historically been important for trade and cultural exchanges between these districts. 

**Trekking and Adventure:**
Traversing Chankheli Pass is considered a challenging endeavor due to its steep ascents and descents. The route offers trekkers an opportunity to experience the rugged beauty of Nepal's far-western Himalayas, including views of the Chankheli Peak, which stands at 4,210 meters. 

**Recent Developments:**
In recent years, infrastructure improvements have enhanced accessibility to the pass. Notably, a jeep has successfully reached Chankheli Pass for the first time over the Mugu-Humla link road, built with UK aid support. 

**Weather Conditions:**
Due to its high elevation, Chankheli Pass experiences variable weather conditions. Travelers should be prepared for cold temperatures and potential snowfall, especially during the winter months.

name: Bagarphant Mandali Church(House of Prayers)
description:
Bagarphant Mandali Church (House of Prayers) is a well-known church located in Jaljala, Bagarphant, Nepal. The church serves as a place of worship and spiritual solace for local Christian communities.

Key Features:
Religious Significance: This church is dedicated to the Christian faith and is a place where locals gather for regular prayers, Sunday services, and other Christian rituals. It offers a serene and peaceful environment for reflection and worship.

Community Events: The church also hosts events for the community, including prayer meetings, Bible studies, and celebrations for Christian holidays such as Christmas and Easter.

Architecture: While specific architectural details may vary, churches in this region often feature a combination of traditional Christian symbols, including crosses and stained glass windows, in their design.

Best Time to Visit:
Sundays: If you wish to experience the church's regular services, Sunday mornings are the most popular time for worship.
Festivals: Celebrations around Christian holidays such as Christmas and Easter attract many visitors, and you may experience special prayers, music, and community events during these times.
Nearby Attractions:
While the church may not be the most famous tourist destination in the area, visitors can enjoy the peaceful and scenic surroundings of Jaljala and Bagarphant. These areas typically feature beautiful landscapes, offering opportunities for hiking, nature walks, or just relaxing in a quiet setting.

name: Aakash Bhairab Mandir
description:
The **Akash Bhairav Temple** is a significant religious site in Nepal, believed to have originally been the palace of the Kiranti King **Yalambar** around 3100 to 3500 years ago. The area surrounding the temple is known as **Yen**, which symbolizes the **Ne** of Nepal, where "Ne" means "Midland" in the Kiranti language. This highlights the deep historical and cultural ties of the site to ancient Nepalese civilizations.

One of the most remarkable aspects of the Akash Bhairav Temple is the head of **Akash Bhairav**, which was unearthed several hundred years ago in Kathmandu. This head is taken out once a year during the **Yenya Festival**, which typically takes place in August or September. During the festival, the head is blessed by the **Kumari**, the living goddess residing in nearby Basantapur. This annual ceremony draws a large number of worshippers who offer **Peda** (sweets made from milk), flowers, money, and other items as part of their devotion.

The Akash Bhairav Temple holds a special place in Nepalese history, with the royal family showing respect for the deity. In the past, the kings of Nepal, including **King Gyanendra** and **King Birendra**, have participated in the ceremonial exchange of swords with the Akash Bhairav, offering deep reverence to this historic icon. The temple and its rituals reflect the rich cultural and spiritual heritage of Nepal, drawing both local devotees and visitors alike to witness the ceremonies and pay homage to the ancient deity.

name: Rolpa Sunchhahari Jharana
description:
Sunchhahari Waterfall, also known as the Golden Waterfall of Rolpa, is a prominent natural attraction located in the Sunchhahari area of Rolpa District, Nepal. This waterfall is renowned for its impressive height and the picturesque landscapes that surround it.

Location and Accessibility

Situated in the Sunchhahari Gaupalika region, the waterfall is accessible via a trek from the nearby town of Jiri. The journey to the waterfall offers trekkers an opportunity to experience the serene beauty of the Rolpa District, characterized by its lush greenery, diverse flora and fauna, and traditional villages.

Trekking Experience

The trek to Sunchhahari Waterfall is considered moderately challenging, making it suitable for trekkers with a reasonable level of fitness. Along the way, trekkers can enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding hills and valleys, providing a refreshing escape from urban life.

Best Time to Visit

The ideal time to visit Sunchhahari Waterfall is during the dry seasons, typically from October to April, when the weather is clear and the trekking paths are accessible. During the monsoon season, the trails can become slippery and challenging due to heavy rainfall.

Cultural Significance

The Sunchhahari area is home to various ethnic communities, each with its unique traditions and lifestyles. Visitors to the waterfall can also explore the local culture, interact with the residents, and gain insights into the traditional way of life in this part of Nepal.

name: Budhanilkantha Temple
description:
Budhanilkantha Temple, situated at the base of Shivapuri Hill in Kathmandu Valley, Nepal, is a revered Hindu shrine dedicated to Lord Vishnu. The temple is renowned for its remarkable 5-meter-long reclining statue of Vishnu, crafted from a single block of black basalt stone. This statue, believed to be over 1,400 years old, is positioned in a pool of water, symbolizing Vishnu's repose on the cosmic ocean. 

Key Features:

Reclining Vishnu Statue: The centerpiece of the temple is the colossal statue of Vishnu in a reclining posture, adorned with a crown and holding the Sudarshana Chakra, a conch shell, a club, and a gem in his four hands. The statue's intricate carvings and serene expression make it a significant attraction for both devotees and tourists. 

Religious Significance: Budhanilkantha Temple holds profound importance in Hinduism. It is especially significant during the Haribondhini Ekadashi Mela, an annual festival observed on the 11th day of the Hindu month of Kartika (October–November). This festival marks the awakening of Lord Vishnu from his long slumber, and the temple becomes a focal point for thousands of pilgrims who gather to participate in rituals and celebrations. 

Cultural Harmony: While primarily a Hindu temple, Budhanilkantha is also venerated by Buddhists. The name "Budhanilkantha" translates to "Blue-Throated Buddha," referring to one of the manifestations of Avalokiteshvara, highlighting the religious harmony present in the region.

name: Khaptad National Park Entry gate
description:
Khaptad National Park is a protected area located in the far western region of Nepal, encompassing parts of the Bajura, Doti, and Achham districts. The park is renowned for its rich biodiversity, including various species of flora and fauna, and its cultural significance.

Entry Points:

The primary entry point to Khaptad National Park is near Silgadhi Bazaar in the Doti District. From Silgadhi, visitors typically embark on a trek to reach the park's headquarters and explore its diverse landscapes. The journey from Silgadhi to the park entrance involves a hike of approximately 6 hours, followed by an additional 7-8 hours to reach the park headquarters. 


Access Routes:

By Air: Travelers can fly from Nepalgunj to Dipayal. From Dipayal, local buses are available to Silgadhi.

By Road: Alternatively, one can drive to Dipayal and then proceed to Silgadhi by road.

Trekking: From Silgadhi, the trek to the park entrance involves navigating through diverse terrains, including forests and meadows.

Facilities:

Accommodation: The park does not have lodges or hotels within its premises. Trekkers are required to be self-sufficient, carrying their own tents, food, fuel, and other necessary supplies.

Permits: Visitors are required to register and pay an entrance fee at the park's entry point.

Best Time to Visit:

The ideal time to visit Khaptad National Park is during the dry seasons, from April to October, when the weather is favorable for trekking and exploration.

name: Vatsala Devi Temple
description:
The Vatsala Devi Temple, also known as the Vatsala Devi Mandir, is a revered Hindu temple situated in Bhaktapur Durbar Square, Kathmandu Valley, Nepal. Dedicated to Goddess Vatsala Devi, an incarnation of Goddess Durga, the temple is renowned for its intricate architecture and historical significance.

**Historical Significance:**

Constructed during the Malla period, the Vatsala Devi Temple is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Nepal. The temple was partially destroyed in the 2015 earthquake but has since undergone restoration efforts to preserve its historical integrity. 

**Architectural Features:**

The temple showcases traditional Newar architecture, featuring a pagoda-style structure with intricately carved wooden windows and doors. The courtyard is adorned with stone sculptures and a stone bell, adding to the temple's serene ambiance.

**Visiting Information:**

The Vatsala Devi Temple is open to visitors year-round. While there is no specific entry fee, visitors are encouraged to respect the local customs and traditions. The temple is located within the Bhaktapur Durbar Square, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, which may have its own entry fees.

**Nearby Attractions:**

While visiting the Vatsala Devi Temple, you can also explore other historical sites within Bhaktapur Durbar Square, such as the 55-Window Palace, Vatsala Temple, and the Lion's Gate.

name: Panini Tapobhumi
description:
**Panini Tapobhumi** is a revered Hindu temple site located in the Panena village of Arghakhanchi District, Lumbini Province, Nepal. This sacred place is traditionally believed to be where the ancient Sanskrit grammarian, Sage Panini, performed penance and composed his seminal work, the *Ashtadhyayi*. 

**Key Features:**

- **Historical Significance:** The site is named after Sage Panini, who is credited with standardizing Sanskrit grammar. Legend holds that he meditated here, and Lord Shiva appeared, blessing him with fourteen sutras that formed the foundation of his grammatical treatise. 

- **Cultural Heritage:** Panini Tapobhumi houses several temples and archaeological sites, reflecting the rich cultural and religious heritage of the region. It is considered an important pilgrimage destination for devotees and scholars alike. 

- **Scenic Beauty:** Situated on a high hill, the area offers panoramic views of the surrounding landscapes, making it a serene spot for visitors seeking both spiritual solace and natural beauty. 

**Visitor Information:**

- **Location:** Panena Village, Arghakhanchi District, Lumbini Province, Nepal.

- **Access:** The site is accessible via local roads from the district headquarters, but visitors are advised to check current travel conditions and seek local guidance for the best routes.

- **Best Time to Visit:** The region experiences a temperate climate, with the dry season from October to April being ideal for visits.

name: Ranipokhari of Bhaktapur
description:
Ranipokhari, also known as the Queen's Pond, is a historic artificial pond located in the heart of Kathmandu, Nepal. Constructed in 1670 by King Pratap Malla in memory of his son, the pond features a central temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, known as the Balgopaleshwor Temple. The pond is surrounded by a stone wall adorned with statues of elephants, symbolizing the king and his sons. Ranipokhari holds significant cultural importance and is a popular site for religious rituals and festivals, including the annual Chhath festival. In 2015, the pond suffered damage due to an earthquake, but reconstruction efforts were completed in October 2020, restoring its historical and cultural significance. 

In addition to its historical significance, Ranipokhari has been a center for various cultural activities. During the Malla period, it served as a venue for royal ceremonies and public gatherings. The pond's design, with its central temple and surrounding statues, reflects the architectural and artistic achievements of the era. The restoration project aimed to preserve these elements while ensuring the pond's structural integrity for future generations. 

Today, Ranipokhari stands as a testament to Nepal's rich cultural heritage, attracting both locals and tourists who come to admire its beauty and historical significance. The pond continues to be a site for various cultural events and religious ceremonies, maintaining its role as a central landmark in Kathmandu.

name: Ananta Bhumi
description:
Ananta Bhumi, located in Rukum East, Nepal, is a region known for its natural beauty and cultural significance. While specific details about "Ananta Bhumi" are limited, Rukum East itself is renowned for its picturesque landscapes, including the Rukumkot valley, which offers stunning views of the surrounding mountains and forests.

Features and Attractions:

Scenic Landscapes: The area is characterized by lush greenery, rolling hills, and panoramic views of the Himalayas, making it a haven for nature enthusiasts and photographers.

Cultural Heritage: Rukum East is home to diverse ethnic communities, each with its unique traditions, festivals, and lifestyles, providing visitors with rich cultural experiences.

Adventure Opportunities: The region offers various trekking routes, allowing adventurers to explore remote villages, interact with local communities, and experience the untouched beauty of the Himalayas.

Visitor Information:

Accessibility: Rukum East is accessible via local transportation from nearby towns and cities. The journey offers scenic views of the countryside, enhancing the travel experience.

Best Time to Visit: The ideal time to visit is during the spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November) seasons when the weather is pleasant, and the skies are clear.

Accommodation: Basic lodging facilities are available in the region, ranging from guesthouses to homestays, offering visitors a chance to experience local hospitality.

name: Bhandarkhal pokhari
description:
Bhandarkhal Pokhari, also known as Kamal Pokhari, is a historic pond situated within the Patan Durbar Square premises in Lalitpur, Nepal. Constructed in the late 17th century, it served as the primary water supply for Patan's royal palace. The pond is approximately 16 meters square in plan. 

The pond is surrounded by ancient architecture, enhancing the beauty of the landmark and serving as a charming backdrop for the famous Durbar Square area. Its presence adds to the cultural and architectural heritage of Patan, attracting both tourists and locals alike. 

On one side of the pond, there is a terrace of very artistic style, where the queen and the priest's wife and friends used to sit and enjoy the pond. The king used to feed fish in the pond from this terrace. The terrace also features various artworks, including 16th-century Christian art on one side. The roof of the terrace is made of fine wood. 

In 2012, the pond underwent restoration efforts after it had dried up, reviving its historical significance and beauty. 

Bhandarkhal Pokhari stands as a testament to the rich history and architectural prowess of the Malla period, offering visitors a serene environment to reflect and explore within the bustling city of Lalitpur.

For those interested in visiting, Bhandarkhal Pokhari is located within the Patan Durbar Square, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, making it easily accessible for tourists exploring the cultural landmarks of the Kathmandu Valley.

name: Sworgadwari Temple, Todkey (Guthi), Kuhun-2, Myagdi
description:
Sworgadwari Temple, located in Todkey (Guthi), Kuhun-2, Myagdi District, Nepal, is a revered Hindu temple situated at an elevation of approximately 2,121 meters above sea level. 

Key Features:

Spiritual Significance: Sworgadwari Temple is considered a major pilgrimage site in Nepal, attracting devotees who seek blessings and spiritual solace. 

Scenic Beauty: The temple offers panoramic views of the surrounding landscapes, including the majestic Himalayas, lush forests, and serene valleys, making it a picturesque destination for visitors.

Cultural Heritage: The temple complex reflects traditional Nepali architecture and serves as a cultural hub, hosting various religious ceremonies and festivals throughout the year.

Visitor Experience:

Pilgrimage: Devotees visit Sworgadwari Temple to perform religious rituals, seek blessings, and participate in community prayers.

Trekking: The journey to the temple involves a trek through scenic trails, offering opportunities to experience the natural beauty and biodiversity of the region.

Photography: The temple's architecture, combined with the stunning natural backdrop, provides ample opportunities for photography enthusiasts.

Practical Information:

Best Time to Visit: The ideal times to visit are during the dry seasons, from October to April, when the weather is favorable for travel and outdoor activities.

Accommodation: Basic lodging options are available in the nearby areas of Myagdi District.

name: Palung Gadhi
description:
Palung Gadhi, situated in the Palungtar Municipality of Gorkha District, Nepal, is a historical site renowned for its strategic significance during the unification of Nepal in the 18th century. The term "Gadhi" refers to a fort or stronghold, and Palung Gadhi served as a crucial military base for King Prithvi Narayan Shah's forces.

The fort's strategic location allowed for effective control over the surrounding regions, playing a pivotal role in the unification campaign. Today, Palung Gadhi stands as a testament to Nepal's rich history, attracting visitors interested in exploring its historical significance and the scenic beauty of the surrounding area.

While specific details about a museum at Palung Gadhi are limited, the site itself offers valuable insights into Nepal's military history and the unification efforts of the 18th century. Visitors can explore the remnants of the fortifications and enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding landscapes.

For those interested in a more comprehensive historical experience, the nearby Palpa Durbar & Museum in Tansen provides a rich collection of artifacts and exhibits related to the region's history and culture. This museum offers a deeper understanding of the historical context of sites like Palung Gadhi.

In summary, Palung Gadhi is a significant historical site in Nepal, offering visitors a glimpse into the country's unification history and the strategic military operations of the 18th century.

name: Rato Machchhindranath Mandir
description:
The Rato Machchhindranath Mandir is a significant religious site located in a large courtyard called Ta Baha, about 400 meters south of Patan's (Lalitpur's) Darbar Square. This temple is dedicated to Machhendranath (also known as Matsyendra), a prominent yogi from the 10th century, who considered the god Shiva his teacher and practiced in the Indic regions of that era.

The current temple, built in 1673, is situated on the foundations of earlier temples dating back to the 15th century. It features a towering Newar-style pagoda with three declining roofs, each covered in sheet metal (possibly copper). The structure is supported by 20 struts on the first and second levels, and 12 on the upper level. Each of the 52 struts is adorned with depictions of Avalokitevara, a bodhisattva, shown in different poses, with some of the figures featuring multiple sets of arms. At the lower registers of the struts, there are miniature scenes illustrating scenarios from Buddhist hells, such as people being boiled alive. Other vignettes show more peaceful scenes with deities supporting Avalokitevara.

The north-facing side of the temple is decorated with an array of pots and pans mounted to tables in a gravity-defying manner, a typical feature of Newar pagodas. A long pataka strip, hanging from the top of the temple to nearly ground level, allows the deity to descend to earth during rituals, adding to the temple's spiritual significance and awe-inspiring design.

name: Bagare Ganesh Temple
description:
The Bagare Ganesh Temple holds spiritual and cultural significance for the local community and Hindu devotees. This temple is dedicated to Lord Ganesha, the elephant-headed deity, who is revered as the remover of obstacles and the god of wisdom and prosperity.

Historical and Cultural Significance:
The exact history of the Bagare Ganesh Temple is not widely documented, but it is likely to have been established as a local place of worship for the surrounding communities. Many small temples like this one were built in Nepal during the medieval era to serve as centers for spiritual gatherings, rituals, and festivals.

Over time, temples dedicated to Lord Ganesha have become important venues for starting new ventures, with worshippers seeking blessings before embarking on significant life events, such as marriage, business endeavors, or other undertakings. In Hindu tradition, Ganesha is believed to ensure that there are no hurdles in these endeavors.

Best Time to Visit:
Festivals: The best time to visit Bagare Ganesh Temple is during Ganesh Chaturthi, the festival dedicated to Lord Ganesha, which typically occurs in late summer or early autumn (August-September). During this festival, temples are decorated, and large processions with idols of Ganesha take place.
Morning & Evening: These are ideal times to visit for a peaceful experience, as the temple is less crowded during these hours, and you can observe the rituals in a more intimate setting.

name: Phewa Lake
description:
Phewa Lake, also known as Fewa Lake, is a prominent freshwater lake situated in the Pokhara Valley of Nepal. As the second-largest lake in Nepal, it spans approximately 4.43 square kilometers and reaches depths of up to 24 meters. The lake is renowned for its serene waters that mirror the surrounding Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges, creating a picturesque landscape. 

A notable feature of Phewa Lake is the Tal Barahi Temple, dedicated to the Hindu goddess Barahi. This two-story pagoda-style temple is situated on a small island in the lake and is accessible by boat. The temple serves as a significant cultural and religious site, attracting both pilgrims and tourists. 

Visitors to Phewa Lake can engage in various activities, including boating, fishing, and exploring the lakeside promenade known as Lakeside. The area is lined with numerous cafes, restaurants, and shops, offering a vibrant atmosphere for relaxation and entertainment. Additionally, the nearby Rani Ban (Queen's Forest) provides opportunities for nature walks and birdwatching. 

For those interested in panoramic views of the lake and the surrounding mountains, a hike up to the World Peace Pagoda is recommended. The pagoda offers breathtaking vistas and a tranquil environment for meditation and reflection. 

Phewa Lake's combination of natural beauty, cultural significance, and recreational opportunities makes it a must-visit destination for travelers exploring Nepal.

name: Kaudena Bahram Temple
description:
The Kaudena Bahram Temple is a Zoroastrian fire temple located in Nepal. It serves as a place of worship for the Zoroastrian community, following the ancient traditions of fire veneration. The temple is dedicated to Atash Bahram, meaning "Victorious Fire," which is one of the highest-grade fires in Zoroastrianism. This sacred fire is consecrated by sixteen different sources, including the fire created by a lightning bolt. 
Key Features:

Architecture: The temple is constructed in traditional Zoroastrian architectural style, featuring a central fire altar where the sacred fire is maintained. The design reflects the ancient Persian influence, with a focus on simplicity and functionality.

Sacred Fire: The Atash Bahram fire is central to the temple's rituals and is kept burning continuously, symbolizing the presence of Ahura Mazda, the supreme deity in Zoroastrianism.

Cultural Significance: The Kaudena Bahram Temple serves as a spiritual center for the Zoroastrian community in Nepal, preserving and promoting their religious practices and cultural heritage.

Visiting Information:

Location: The temple is situated in a serene environment, offering visitors a peaceful atmosphere for reflection and prayer.

Access: Visitors are welcome to observe the rituals and learn about Zoroastrian traditions. It is advisable to contact the temple authorities in advance to arrange a visit and to understand any specific guidelines or customs to be followed.

name: Bhedetar View Tower
description:
Bhedetar, a serene hill station in Nepal's Koshi Province, is renowned for its breathtaking vistas and pleasant climate. A highlight of this destination is the **Bhedetar Skywalk Tower**, formerly known as Charles Point or Shailung Danda. This viewpoint earned the name "Charles Point" after Prince Charles of the UK visited in the 1980s and admired the panoramic views of the Himalayas, including peaks like Mt. Kumbhakarna, Mt. Makalu, Mt. Kanchenjunga, and Mt. Everest. 

The original multistoried tower, accessible via a spiral staircase, offered visitors expansive views of up to sixteen districts from its summit. However, following the 2015 earthquake, the structure was closed due to safety concerns. 

In recent years, the site has undergone significant redevelopment. As of July 2024, the area has been transformed into the **Bhedetar Skywalk Tower**, featuring a modern skywalk design that allows visitors to experience the landscape from a unique vantage point. This redevelopment aims to boost tourism by providing a safe and exhilarating experience for visitors. 

Bhedetar's strategic location, approximately 16 kilometers from Dharan and 52 kilometers from Biratnagar, makes it a popular destination for both domestic and international tourists seeking respite from the heat of the Terai region. The hill station's unpredictable weather adds to its charm, with moments of thick fog followed by clear skies revealing stunning landscapes.

name: Dhunge Dhara Bode
description:
Dhunge Dhara Bode is a traditional stone spout, or 'dhunge dhara,' located in the Bode area of Madhyapur Thimi, Nepal. These stone spouts are integral to Nepalese culture, serving as communal water sources and reflecting the country's rich architectural heritage.

Key Features:

Historical Significance: Dhunge dharas have been utilized for centuries, providing potable water to local communities. They are considered symbols of communal life and traditional engineering.

Architectural Design: Typically constructed from stone, these structures feature intricately carved spouts and basins. The design often includes a series of steps leading down to the water source, facilitating easy access for users.

Cultural Importance: Beyond their functional role, dhunge dharas are cultural landmarks, often associated with local festivals and rituals. They serve as gathering spots for community interaction and socialization.

Visitor Information:

Accessibility: Bode is accessible by road from Kathmandu, with a drive time of approximately 30 minutes. The Dhunge Dhara Bode is situated within the town, making it easily reachable for visitors.

Nearby Attractions: Visitors can explore other historical sites in Madhyapur Thimi, such as the Bhaktapur Durbar Square and the ancient temples of Changunarayan.

Best Time to Visit: The ideal time to visit is during the dry season, from October to April, when the weather is clear and conducive to sightseeing.

name: Balkumari Mandir
description:
Balkumari Temple, located in Lalitpur District, Nepal, is a revered Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Balkumari, considered a manifestation of the Astamatrikas. The temple's origins are debated, with estimates ranging from the 7th to the 17th century. 

Historical Significance:

Architecture: The temple showcases traditional Newari pagoda-style architecture, featuring intricate wood carvings and multiple tiers. 

Cultural Events: Balkumari Temple serves as the starting point for the Pyakhaa Jatra festival, which concludes after three days in Sunakothi. This festival typically occurs about a month after Holi. 

Visitor Experience:

Spiritual Atmosphere: Devotees and visitors can immerse themselves in the temple's serene environment, observing traditional rituals and practices.

Cultural Insight: The temple offers a glimpse into the rich cultural heritage of the Newar community, with various deities' idols adorning the temple walls. 

Practical Information:

Location: Approximately 800 meters east of Patan Durbar Square, making it accessible for visitors exploring the area. 

Visiting Hours: While specific visiting hours are not detailed, it's advisable to visit during daylight hours to fully appreciate the temple's architecture and surroundings.

Restoration Efforts: The temple has undergone several restorations due to damage from earthquakes and other factors, reflecting the community's dedication to preserving this sacred site.

name: Kopan Monastery
description:
Religious Site Kopan Monastery, nestled near Boudhanath on the outskirts of Kathmandu, Nepal, is a haven for Tibetan Buddhist study and practice. Founded in 1969 by Lama Thubten Yeshe and Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Kopan has garnered international acclaim for its dedication to teaching Buddhism to Westerners.
More than just a monastery, Kopan has blossomed into a complex encompassing two distinct institutions: the Kopan Monastery atop Kopan Hill and the nearby Khachoe Ghakyil Ling Nunnery, established in 1979 to empower women with spiritual and practical education modelled after the monks' program. The nunnery's remarkable growth, from 4 nuns to 400 in under 35 years, is a testament to its dedication and the generosity of supporters who utilize platforms like GoFundMe to fuel its expansion.
Beyond its educational pursuits, Kopan Monastery has become a vibrant community hub, welcoming hundreds of visitors every Saturday from 10 AM to 4 PM. While closed to the public on weekdays, these designated hours offer Kathmandu residents and tourists alike a chance to immerse themselves in the monastery's serene atmosphere, participate in guided meditations, and soak in the wisdom dispensed by resident monks and teachers. Kopan Monastery stands as a beacon of Buddhist scholarship and spiritual practice, attracting both dedicated students and curious travelers seeking a glimpse into the rich tapestry of Tibetan Buddhist culture.

name: Doleshwar Mahadev Temple
description:
Religious Site The Doleshwar temple is constructed in pagoda style. The temple is also known as Bimaleshwor and Sipare Mahadev and other names as per the local tongue and tradition. Inside the temple, there is a huge plain Shiva Linga (phallus). There are taps, a big idol of bull, a tall Trishul and other artifacts around with some constructions still underway.

Visiting this Shiva temple and offering milk and bel leaves to Lord Shiva is an important ritual for the Hindus or Lord Shiva devotees. The place which was unknown for thousands of years can be now called as a hidden gem. With the grace of Lord Shiva, it is an immense opportunity for the devotees to visit this sacred site and be blessed for the life time.

When you plan to visit Doleshwar, you can also visit other Shiva shrines like Ashapuri Mahadev Temple and Sanga, which are only few kilometers away. Sanga consists of Kailashnath Mahadev which is the world s tallest statue to Lord Shiva, standing 44 meters tall on a high hill. It can be an ideal day trip to visit all these shrines on a single day which can provide you an inner peace and evoke faith on god.

Doleshwar Mahadev is a temple of glory to all Hindu devotees around the world, and one must visit here to gain the ultimate religious experience, as some claim, the great opportunity to worship both the body and the head part of Lord Shiva is obtained only by the virtue acquired from multiple births.

name: Bhimsen Mandir
description:
The **Bhimsen Temple** is a significant Hindu temple located in **Patan Durbar Square**, Kathmandu Valley, Nepal. Dedicated to **Bhimsen**, the deity revered as the god of trade among the Newar community, the temple holds a central position in the square, adjacent to the Vishwanath Temple and opposite the Mani Mandapa pavilions. 

**Historical Background:**

The temple's origins are uncertain, but it was reconstructed in 1682 by King Shrinivas Malla following a fire. Subsequent reconstructions occurred in 1934 after the great earthquake and again in 1967. Although the temple sustained significant damage in the April 2015 earthquake, it reopened in early 2022 after extensive reconstruction, retaining much of its pre-earthquake form. 

**Architectural Features:**

The Bhimsen Temple is renowned for its distinctive architecture, including three interconnected golden windows. The temple's design reflects traditional Newar architectural styles, characterized by intricate wood carvings and ornate decorations. 

**Visiting the Temple:**

Visitors to the Bhimsen Temple can explore its rich history and architectural beauty. The temple is an integral part of Patan Durbar Square, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, which also features other notable structures such as the Vishwanath Temple and the Krishna Mandir. The square is a hub of cultural and religious activities, offering a glimpse into Nepal's rich heritage.

name: B. P. Park
description:
**B. P. Park**, located in Ilam, Nepal, is a serene and picturesque destination that offers visitors a tranquil environment to relax and enjoy nature. Situated in the eastern region of Nepal, Ilam is renowned for its lush tea gardens, rolling hills, and vibrant cultural heritage.

- **Natural Beauty:** The park is surrounded by verdant landscapes, providing a peaceful retreat for nature enthusiasts and those seeking respite from urban life.

- **Cultural Significance:** Ilam is known for its rich cultural heritage, and the park serves as a hub for local events and gatherings, offering visitors a glimpse into the traditions and lifestyle of the region.

- **Tea Gardens:** The area is famous for its tea plantations, and visitors can explore the nearby tea estates to learn about the tea-making process and enjoy fresh brews.

name: Ratna Park
description:
Ratna Park, situated in the heart of Kathmandu, Nepal, is a cherished green space that offers a tranquil retreat amidst the city's vibrant atmosphere. Established in honor of Queen Ratna, the wife of King Mahendra, the park serves as a central hub for both locals and tourists seeking relaxation and leisure. 

Covering approximately 22,000 square meters, Ratna Park features well-maintained gardens, winding pathways, and a central fountain, creating a serene environment for visitors. The park is adorned with lush gardens, winding pathways, and a collection of native plants, making it an ideal spot for relaxation or a leisurely stroll. 

Beyond its natural beauty, Ratna Park is a vibrant social hub. The surrounding area is lined with shops and food stalls, offering a variety of local snacks and refreshments. Visitors can often find families enjoying picnics, couples taking romantic walks, or tourists simply resting on benches while soaking in the surroundings. 

Ratna Park's central location, nestled between Rani Pokhari and Tudikhel, makes it easily accessible and a popular destination for those looking to experience the hustle and bustle of Kathmandu while enjoying a peaceful environment. 

Whether you're seeking a peaceful retreat, a family outing, or a picturesque location for photographs, Ratna Park is a delightful destination that encapsulates the natural beauty and cultural heritage of Nepal.

name: Baidhyanath Dham Temple
description:
Baidhyanath Dham Temple, also known as Baidhyanath Temple, is a revered Hindu shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva, located in the Achham District of Nepal. Situated at the confluence of the Budhi Ganga and Saraswati rivers, the temple holds significant religious importance and is a prominent pilgrimage site. 

**Location and Accessibility:**
The temple is located at coordinates 6673+8JJ, Manadaira, Baidyanath, 10700, Nepal. Visitors can reach the temple by traveling to the Achham District, with local transportation options available from nearby towns.

**Historical and Cultural Significance:**
Baidhyanath Dham is mentioned in the Skanda Purana, highlighting its ancient roots and the legend of Lord Shiva granting Ravana nine heads at this site.  The temple complex houses a school called Ved Vidyashram, dedicated to the study of Vedic scriptures. In 2020, the government allocated NPR 2 million to upgrade the Ved Vidyashram, reflecting the site's cultural and educational importance. 

**Festivals and Events:**
The temple attracts numerous pilgrims, especially during the festival of Shivaratri, when devotees from Nepal and India visit to offer prayers and participate in religious activities. 

**Visitor Information:**
For those planning a visit, it is advisable to check local resources or contact community centers in the Achham District for the latest information on temple activities and accessibility.

name: Jayakriti Mahavihar (Thathu Bahi)
description:
Heritage Site Jayakriti Mahavihar, also known as Thatu Bahi is one of the most prominent vihars of Bhaktapur. Each year, Samyak Panchadan like-substantial event takes place over there.
It is located at Itachhen, on the western arena of the Na: Pukhu (Guhyepokhari of Bhaktapur). A two-storeyed building made out of a traditional Nepalese style (currently functioning as a Shree Gyan Bijaya Primary School) is also the house of one of the Dipankar Buddhas of Bhaktapur.
There is a beautiful courtyard inside the building where one can find small chaityas and stupa along with exquisite woodâ€™s working and the image of Padmapani Lokeshwora, the central deity of the Bahi.
The vihar is placed in the highland, thatâ€™s why it is called thatu Bahi.
The vihar, as mentioned in the inscriptions and scriptures ascertains that it is way older than other vihars. The presence of two Chaityas and a gate with Panchabuddha summarises that it was made in the Lichhavi era.
There is even some chatter saying Na: Pukhu was later made on the land of Thathu Bahi.
It is said that the vihar was also renovated by King Jitamitra Malla and Ugra Malla after Jaya Ratna Bajracharya, who was a member of Chatur Varna Mahavihar.
The mentioned date when Jaya Ratna Bajracharya renovated it was N.S.794 and only after that, the Thatu Bahi was started to call Jayakriti Mahavihar. Moreover, it still seems to be in a good condition.

name: Khanivanjyang Okhaldhunga
description:
hanivanjyang is a village located in the Manebhanjyang Rural Municipality within the Okhaldhunga District of Province No. 1, Nepal. Manebhanjyang was established on March 10, 2017, by merging several Village Development Committees (VDCs), including Moli, Baksa, Nepal, Ubu, Ketuke, Manebhanjyang, Thakle, Thoksela, and Madhavpur. 


Geographical Location:

Khanivanjyang is situated in the eastern region of Nepal, approximately 125 kilometers east of Kathmandu, the capital city. The village is accessible via the Manebhanjyang-Galchhi Road, which connects to the Prithvi Highway at Malekhu, facilitating transportation to and from Khanivanjyang.

Demographics:

As of the 2011 Nepal census, Manebhanjyang Rural Municipality had a population of 21,093. The population is diverse, with various ethnic groups, including Rai, Magar, Chhetri, Newar, Tamang, Hill Brahmin, and others. 


Economic Activities:

Agriculture is the primary livelihood for the residents of Khanivanjyang. The municipality has prioritized coffee farming, providing grants to farmers to boost production and improve economic conditions. 


Cultural Significance:

Khanivanjyang, along with the rest of Manebhanjyang Rural Municipality, is known for its rich cultural heritage, including traditional customs, festivals, and practices. The area offers opportunities for eco-tourism, including trekking and exploring local traditions.

name: Annapurna Temple
description:
The Heritage Site located behind the Shiddi Laxmi Temple, commonly referred to as Lohan Dega, is a fascinating and mysterious temple, often called the "Temple of Annapurna." This temple has sparked much intrigue due to its unusual structure and the various names associated with it. Many locals and visitors are uncertain of its true identity, with some suggesting that it is dedicated to Goddess Annapurna, while others claim that it houses a Sriyantra, a tantric symbol linked to Goddess Vatsala Devi, and still others believe it could be a temple for Annapurna.

One striking feature of this temple is its architectural design. Traditionally, the temple is said to have had doors on all four sides. However, in its current state, these doors have been replaced by brick walls, leaving only a single door on the southern side. The presence of these walls has contributed to the temple’s sense of mystery.

The structure’s history is also significant. An inscription found on the pedestal of the Sriyantra suggests that the temple dates back to N.S. 816 (which corresponds to Thursday, February 20, 1996 A.D.), giving it a rich historical and cultural background.

Despite the uncertainty surrounding its exact purpose and name, the "Temple of Annapurna" remains an important and revered site for locals and visitors alike, providing a glimpse into Nepal's rich architectural and spiritual heritage.

name: Jagadulla Taal
description:
Jagadulla Taal, also known as Jagadulla Lake, is a pristine freshwater lake situated at an elevation of approximately 4,700 meters above sea level in the Jagadulla Rural Municipality of Dolpa District, Nepal. This secluded lake is renowned for its unique heart-shaped appearance, earning it the nickname "Prem Taal" or "Heart Lake.Geographical Features:

Location: Jagadulla Taal is nestled in the remote regions of Dolpa, a district known for its rugged terrain and rich cultural heritage. The lake is accessible via challenging trekking routes, making it a destination for adventurous travelers.

Altitude: At 4,700 meters, the lake is situated in the high-altitude zone, offering breathtaking views of the surrounding Himalayan landscapes.Cultural Significance:

The lake holds religious importance for both Buddhist and Hindu communities in the region. It was historically known as Dudh Kunda and later as Rakxes Daha before being referred to as Prem Taal due to its heart-shaped form.Trekking and Accessibility:

Trekking Routes: Reaching Jagadulla Taal involves a strenuous trek through rugged terrains, requiring proper preparation and acclimatization. The journey offers trekkers a chance to experience the untouched natural beauty of Dolpa.

Best Time to Visit: The ideal time to visit is during the dry season, from October to April, when the weather is clear and suitable for trekking.

name: Bhairavanath temple
description:
Bhairavanath Temple, situated in Bhaktapur's Taumadhi Square, is a significant Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Bhairava, a fierce manifestation of Lord Shiva. The temple's history dates back to the 13th century, with King Ananda Deva believed to have inaugurated it. Over the centuries, it has undergone several renovations, notably by King Bhupatindra Malla in the early 18th century, who transformed it into a three-tiered structure adorned with seven golden pinnacles. 

Architecturally, the temple is rectangular, featuring a pagoda-style roof with intricate wood carvings. It stands adjacent to the Nyatapola Temple, another architectural marvel of Bhaktapur. The temple's design reflects the rich Newar architectural tradition, characterized by detailed woodwork and tiered roofs. 

An intriguing legend associated with the temple narrates that Lord Bhairava once visited Bhaktapur to witness the Bisket Jatra festival. Recognized by a priest, Lord Bhairava attempted to return to Varanasi but was detained. In the ensuing struggle, the priest decapitated him, leading to the belief that the head of the idol does not match its body. 

Visitors to Bhairavanath Temple can explore its rich history, admire its architectural beauty, and experience the vibrant atmosphere of Taumadhi Square. The temple remains a central place of worship and a testament to Bhaktapur's cultural heritage.

name: Babarmahal Palace
description:
Babarmahal Palace, also known as Babar Mahal Revisited, is a historical landmark located in the heart of Kathmandu, Nepal, near the Singha Durbar government offices. Originally built in the late 19th century by Chandra Sekhar Jang Bahadur Rana, the palace served as a royal residence during the Rana period. Reflecting the grand architectural style of the time, it has been meticulously preserved and renovated to retain its historical charm while adapting it for modern use.

Today, Babarmahal Revisited is a vibrant heritage complex that blends historical significance with contemporary amenities. It features a variety of shops, restaurants, and cultural spaces, making it a bustling commercial hub. The serene environment of the complex offers a peaceful respite from the busy streets of Kathmandu, with visitors able to explore upscale dining options, artisanal boutiques, and art galleries.

The complex not only functions as a commercial venue but also serves as a museum, showcasing the architectural legacy of the Rana period and Nepal's cultural history. It has become a popular destination for both locals and tourists, offering a unique opportunity to experience the intersection of Kathmandu's past and present.

Babar Mahal remains a key symbol of the city's architectural beauty and cultural evolution, making it a must-visit spot for those interested in Nepal's rich heritage.

name: Bhaktapur Durbar Square
description:
Bhaktapur Durbar Square, also known as Layaku, is a historic plaza located in the heart of Bhaktapur, Nepal. This UNESCO World Heritage Site was once the royal palace complex of the Malla kings from the 14th to 15th centuries and later the kings of the Kingdom of Bhaktapur until the late 18th century. The square is renowned for its medieval art and architecture, featuring numerous pagoda and shikhara-style temples, intricate wood carvings, and statues of kings atop stone monoliths. Despite suffering damage from earthquakes, including those in 1833, 1934, and 2015, many structures have been restored, preserving the square's historical significance. 

Visitors to Bhaktapur Durbar Square can explore notable landmarks such as the 55-Window Palace, Vatsala Temple, and the statues of the Malla kings. The square also serves as a vibrant hub for local artisans, offering a glimpse into traditional Newar culture and craftsmanship. The area is lined with traditional houses, handicraft shops, and eateries, providing a rich cultural experience. 

For those interested in accommodations, Hotel Layaku Durbar is a 3-star hotel situated near the square, offering convenient access to the city's major attractions. 

Whether you're a history enthusiast, art lover, or simply looking to immerse yourself in Nepalese culture, Bhaktapur Durbar Square offers a unique and enriching experience.

name: Taplejung Samrakshyan Smriti Park
description:

name: Phalelung (Phalut)
description:
Phalelung, also known as Phalut, is a notable peak situated at an elevation of 3,600 meters (11,800 feet) on the Singalila Ridge in the Himalayas. It lies at the tri-junction of Nepal, the Indian state of West Bengal, and the Indian state of Sikkim. This peak is renowned for its panoramic views of some of the world's highest mountains, including Mount Everest, Kangchenjunga, and Lhotse. 

The indigenous tribes in the vicinity have a 300-year history of revering Phalut as an omniscient deity, referring to the peak as "Omna Re Ay." 

Phalelung Rural Municipality, located in Province No. 1 of Nepal, encompasses an area of 207.14 square kilometers and had a population of 21,884 as per the 2011 Census of Nepal. 

The trek to Phalut is celebrated for its scenic beauty, offering trekkers the opportunity to traverse diverse landscapes, including dense forests, alpine meadows, and traditional settlements. The journey along the Singalila Ridge is particularly esteemed for providing some of the most rewarding vistas in the Himalayas. 

For those interested in exploring this region, the Sandakphu-Phalut trek is a popular route that offers breathtaking experiences of the Himalayan ranges. 

Phalelung's rich natural beauty and cultural heritage make it a compelling destination for trekkers, nature enthusiasts, and those seeking spiritual solace amidst the grandeur of the Himalayas.

name: Jaubari
description:
Natural Landmark Jaubari tourist area is the confluence of Maijogmai-2 and Sandakpur Rural Municipality-5. October to April is the peak tourist season in Jaubari. From the Indian side, you can reach Bhanjyang via a pitch road and reach Jaubari in 15 minutes from Tumling, attracting many Indian tourists.
Jaubari is an affordable destination, attracting Bengali tourists from West Bengal, India. Rain in the rainy season, misty fog, and heavy snowfall in winter are major attractions in Jaubari. Upon reaching Jaubari, one can also enjoy watching the glaciers.
There are seven homestays operating in Jaubari to accommodate tourists. There are large and well-organized hotels in Tumling near the Indian border Dashagaja. Electricity and telecommunication services are available in Jaubari. At an altitude of 2,900 meters above sea level, it snows in November and January. Jaubari, which is the habitat of red pandas, sees a large presence of native and foreign wildlife conservation workers.
Tourists who come to reach Sandakpur also return from Jaubari because the sunrise view is exceptional here. Not only the view of sunrise and sunset from Ramite hill of Jaubari but also the view of Mount Kanchenjunga captivates everyone. A part of the highest peak, Everest, can also be seen from here. From Jaubari, one can observe Jhapa district and the cities and rivers of India.

name: Bedkot Lake
description:
Bedkot Lake is a renowned tourist attraction situated in the Bedkot Municipality of Kanchanpur District, Sudurpashchim Province, Nepal. Located approximately 6 kilometers north of Daijee, the lake is nestled at the confluence of the Terai plains and the mountainous regions, offering visitors a unique blend of landscapes. 


Key Features:

Scenic Beauty: The lake is surrounded by lush greenery and rolling hills, providing a serene environment ideal for relaxation and nature walks.

Cultural Significance: Bedkot Lake holds religious importance, particularly among Hindus, and is considered a pilgrimage site. The area is also home to the Shiva Temple, adding to its spiritual allure. 

Accessibility: The lake is accessible via a paved road that extends up to Chure Phedi in Bedkot Municipality-3, enhancing its connectivity and ease of access for tourists. 

Activities:

Picnicking: The tranquil surroundings make it an excellent spot for picnics and family outings.

Photography: The picturesque landscapes offer ample opportunities for photography enthusiasts.

Cultural Exploration: Visitors can explore the nearby Shiva Temple and engage with local communities to learn about regional traditions and customs.

Visiting Information:

Best Time to Visit: The ideal seasons are spring and autumn when the weather is pleasant, and the natural beauty is at its peak.

name: Nil Saraswati Mandir
description:
Religious Site Neel Saraswati Temple, located in Lazimpat, Kathmandu, is a revered Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Neel Saraswati, a form of the goddess Tara. This temple is particularly significant for students and scholars, as it is associated with knowledge and wisdom.
The temple is believed to have been established by Gunakamdev and has roots dating back to the end of the Malla period. The idol of Neel Saraswati has been worshipped by both Hindus and Buddhists, reflecting its cultural significance.
The temple features traditional Nepali architectural styles and includes idols of Saraswati depicted with harps, books, and garlands, symbolizing knowledge and learning.
Neel Saraswati Temple is especially popular during the festival of Basant Panchami (Saraswati Puja), when devotees gather to worship the goddess and seek blessings for academic success. The temple becomes a hub for students during this time.
The temple offers a serene environment conducive to meditation, attracting visitors looking for peace and spiritual reflection.
Situated in a central location in Kathmandu, the temple is easily accessible by public transport and is a popular destination for both locals and tourists.
Overall, Neel Saraswati Temple serves as an important spiritual center in Kathmandu, embodying the rich traditions of Hindu worship and the pursuit of knowledge.

name: Jaljaleswor Mahadev Sthan
description:
The Jaleshwar Mahadev Temple is a revered Hindu shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva, situated in the Mahottari district of Nepal. This temple holds significant religious importance and attracts numerous devotees, especially during major Hindu festivals.

Historical Significance:

The temple is believed to have been established centuries ago, with records indicating its existence since the time of King Janak. It is traditionally associated with the marriage of Lord Rama and Goddess Sita, where soil was taken from this temple. A copper inscription within the temple notes that in AD, King Girvan Yuddha Bikram Shah provided 275 bighas of land to administer the templeArchitecture:

Constructed in the Gumbaja architectural style, the temple features a square Shiva Linga submerged in water at its center. Adjacent to the temple is a pond, enhancing the serene ambiance of the site.Festivals and Events:

The temple is a focal point for religious activities, particularly during festivals such as Maha Shivaratri and Vasant Panchami, drawing pilgrims from various regions.

Visiting Information:

Location: Jaleshwar, Mahottari District, Nepal.

Access: The temple is accessible by road from the district headquarters, Jaleshwar.

Best Time to Visit: While the temple is open year-round, visiting during the aforementioned festivals offers a unique cultural experience.

name: Panch Pokhari
description:
**Panch Pokhari**, meaning "Five Lakes" in Nepali, is a revered pilgrimage site situated at an elevation of approximately 4,100 meters in the Sindhupalchowk District, northeast of Kathmandu Valley. This sacred destination is significant to both Hindus and Buddhists, attracting numerous devotees, especially during the Janai Purnima festival in August.

**Key Features:**

- **Religious Significance:** During Janai Purnima, thousands of pilgrims visit Panch Pokhari to take ritual baths in the lakes, believing it cleanses past sins and fulfills wishes. 

- **Natural Beauty:** The area offers stunning views of the Jugal Himal range, including peaks like Dorje Lakpa, Madiya, and Phurbi Chhyachu. The pristine lakes are surrounded by diverse flora and fauna, making it a haven for nature enthusiasts. 

- **Trekking Experience:** The trek to Panch Pokhari is a rewarding adventure, passing through lush forests, traditional Tamang and Sherpa villages, and offering panoramic mountain vistas. The journey provides insights into the local cultures and lifestyles. 

**Visitor Information:**

- **Location:** Panch Pokhari is located in the Sindhupalchowk District, northeast of Kathmandu Valley, Nepal.

- **Best Time to Visit:** The ideal time for trekking is during the dry season, from October to March, when the weather is favorable for outdoor activities.

name: Agnishala Temple
description:
Agnishala Temple, located in Patan within the Kathmandu Valley, is a revered religious site with a history spanning over 4,000 years. This ancient Hindu temple holds significant importance for devotees seeking to overcome misfortune caused by unfavorable planetary configurations (Graha Dasha). The temple is renowned for its five kundas (fire altars), each named after prominent deities: Vishnu Kunda, Brahma Kunda, Shiva Kunda, Surya Kunda, and Savya Kunda. Of these, Vishnu Kunda is particularly notable for having a continuous (eternal) fire that has been burning for many years.

Devotees visit the temple to perform "hom," a religious ritual involving offerings in the holy fire of Vishnu Kunda, which is believed to bring happiness and well-being. The temple is one of the most important shrines in the Kathmandu Valley, especially during the festival of Maghe Sankranti, which marks the welcoming of spring. During this time, large crowds gather to worship the kundas and the sacred fire. Additionally, Buddha Jayanti, the first day of the month of Kartik, is considered the anniversary of the temple according to the holy priests.

Hindu devotees from all around the world make pilgrimages to Agnishala Temple at least once in their lifetime. If you're visiting the Kathmandu Valley, this historic and spiritually significant temple is worth a visit.

name: Nuwakot Palace
description:
Historical Ruins Nuwakot: A History in Nepal
Nuwakot, nestled on the banks of the Trishuli and Tandi Rivers, boasts a rich tapestry woven with stories of conquest, trade, and political significance. For over a millennium, its hilltop fort served as a watchful guardian, protecting the western entry to Kathmandu Valley. As a bustling hub for the Malla kings, Nuwakot facilitated trade between India and Tibet. Its strategic importance drew covetous eyes, and the fort endured numerous battles, most notably succumbing to a surprise attack by Prithvi Narayan Shah in 1744.
This pivotal victory by Shah marked a turning point in Nepalese history. Nuwakot became a crucial launching pad for Shah's conquest of the Kathmandu Valley, solidifying his kingdom's dominance. The echoes of history resonate further: Nuwakot nearly fell to Chinese forces during the Nepal-China conflict, and witnessed the first diplomatic meeting between Nepal and Britain.
Nuwakot's legacy is preserved in the majestic seven-story Durbar complex, expanded by Shah to cater to flourishing trade routes. The exquisite Malla-style architecture reflects the town's past grandeur, a testament to its role as a center of power and prosperity. In recognition of its significance, Nuwakot seeks inscription as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, ensuring its legacy shines for generations to come.

name: mountain view salyan

name: Khaniyabus Piknic Area
description:
Khaniyabus Picnic Area is a scenic spot located in the Khaniyabus area of Okhaldhunga District, Nepal. Situated approximately 125 kilometers east of Kathmandu, the capital city, Khaniyabus offers a tranquil environment ideal for picnics and relaxation.

Khaniyabus is accessible via the Manebhanjyang-Galchhi Road, connecting to the Prithvi Highway at Malekhu. This road network facilitates transportation to and from Khaniyabus, linking it to other parts of the district and the country.

The picnic area is equipped with basic facilities, including shaded picnic tables and restrooms, providing a comfortable setting for visitors.
